summary: Structure, ontology terms, file coverage (96 Tryp RAW; with the LysC sibling 303/303, no overlap) and the SILAC/SILAM design check out, but comment[cleavage agent details] records Trypsin only, although the *_Tryp_* peptides come from material that was digested with LysC overnight and then with trypsin in the same centricon. That makes it a sequential Lys-C + trypsin digest.

reviewer_context.context: fresh subagent reviewer with no producer transcript; re-fetched PRIDE files/all and project record, re-read the manuscript, streamed the deposited A53T_mutant_rep2 mzid, queried OLS directly

spec_compliance.evidence: 38 columns, 192 rows, all rows 38 fields. Column order and the required columns of the ms-proteomics 1.1.0 + vertebrates 1.1.0 contract (sdrf-tools contract) are present. Reserved words are used only where allowed. (source name, assay name, comment[label]) is unique.

ontology_integrity.evidence: All 19 accessions resolved in OLS4 with exact labels and none obsolete (NCBITaxon:10090, UBERON:0001891, MONDO:0005180, PATO:0000461, EFO:0001272, PRIDE:0000627/0000326/0000325/0000564/0000608/0000599, MS:1001910/1001251/1000422/1000484, UNIMOD:4/35/188/1). No UBERON/BTO term means exactly 'ventral midbrain', so the generalisation to midbrain is justified. The enzyme set is incomplete: Lys-C (MS:1001309) is missing for this sequential digest (finding 1).

source_evidence.evidence: Manuscript (PMC8628316, title and PMID verified) for A53T samples: 'proteins were digested with LysC ... in the centricon at 37 C overnight ... flow-through kept ... Sequencing-grade trypsin ... was added to the centricon'. The deposited mzid (Mouse_SILAM_A53T_mutant_rep2) Enzyme is MS:1001309 LysC for the Tryp files. Every other claim checked holds: one mouse per group, technical duplicate, SILAM 13C6-Lys pool, ventral midbrain, Orbitrap Elite, HCD 32, m/z 350-1550, 10 ppm/0.02 Da, DTT/IAA, strains.

file_mapping.evidence: PRIDE files/all re-fetched (320 entries, all projectAccessions PXD015293, 303 RAW). This SDRF holds exactly the 96 *_Tryp_* RAW and the sibling holds the other 207: the union is 303/303 with zero overlap and nothing invented. The absent mutant_rep2 Tryp F09-F11 are also missing from the deposited mzid SpectraData, so the gap is genuine. The f09a/f10a/f11a sizes (546-616 MB) match the rep1 series, not rep2 (365-477 MB), and rep1 f10/f11 are truncated (133/251 MB). That supports treating them as rep1 re-acquisitions (technical replicate 3).

design_consistency.evidence: Recomputed: 4 sources (2 light mice, 2 per-mixture SILAM heavy aliquots) x 24 fractions x 2 injection series, minus mutant rep2 F09-F11, plus 3 rep1 re-acquisitions = 96 assays x 2 labels. The light/heavy pair shares assay, file, technical replicate and fraction. No collision on (source, biological replicate, technical replicate, fraction). The split by digest is justified: the LysC flow-through and the trypsin retentate are separate peptide pools, each fractionated 1-24 for the same mouse and injection, so a single file would collide or need invented fraction numbers.

omission_safety.evidence: No unsupported additions: sex is 'not available', the pool size is unstated, and the protein N-term Acetyl is confirmed in the mzid (553 acetyl peptides, all PeptideEvidence pre='-'). The material evidence that the Tryp series saw LysC (sequential digest, LysC still in the 30 kDa centricon, search enzyme LysC) is acknowledged only in the manifest limitations and not reflected in the SDRF.

deterministic_validation.evidence: flock parse_sdrf validate-sdrf --template ms-proteomics --template vertebrates: exit 0, warnings only (free-text strain not in NCBITaxon). sdrf-tools check: 17/17 verified, CLEAN, exit 0. sdrf-tools score: 100/100, exit 0. Separate per-template runs did not start (lock contention); the union run covers both templates per the brief.

findings.message: Only NT=Trypsin;AC=MS:1001251 is recorded, but the *_Tryp_* peptides come from a sequential Lys-C + trypsin digest.
findings.evidence: Methods (A53T): LysC overnight in the 30 kDa centricon, LysC flow-through removed (= *_LysC_* series), then trypsin added to the same centricon, where the retained protein had already been exposed to LysC and the enzyme was still present. Deposited mzid Enzyme = MS:1001309 LysC for these files. The campaign brief sanctions a repeated cleavage-agent column for combined digests.
findings.correction: Add a second comment[cleavage agent details] column with NT=Lys-C;AC=MS:1001309 on all 192 rows, keeping Trypsin, or cite evidence that the trypsin-step material was not exposed to LysC.
